note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right middle finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. Hill is a 41-year-old female presenting with pain at the tip of her right middle finger for approximately four to five days. The injury occurred during a motor vehicle accident on Saturday when the patient was struck from behind while stopped at a four-way stop sign. In response to being rear-ended, the patient made a gesturing motion with her right middle finger and struck it against the ceiling of the car. She reports this was the only injury sustained in the accident, which resulted in minor trunk damage to her vehicle. Pain has persisted at the distal tip of the middle finger since the incident.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies any other injuries from the motor vehicle accident. No other systemic complaints documented.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrial fibrillation.

MEDICATIONS
Digoxin for atrial fibrillation.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient was involved in a motor vehicle accident when rear-ended at a four-way stop by another driver believed to be texting while driving.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: 41-year-old female, alert and oriented.
Right hand: Tenderness elicited over the distal phalanx of the right middle finger with palpation. Tenderness is absent over the proximal and middle phalanges. Remainder of exam is normal.

RESULTS
X-ray of right middle finger shows a distal phalanx fracture of the middle finger (third digit).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger secondary to motor vehicle accident.
1. Tramadol 50 mg every six hours as needed for pain; dispense 8 tablets (two days' supply).
2. Place right middle finger in finger splint.
3. Follow-up x-ray in two weeks.
4. Patient counseled that tramadol is safe to take with her current digoxin therapy for atrial fibrillation.
